title: Invalid states: the diagnostic axis, implemented (+ highlighter kinds)
summary: docs/INVALID-STATES-PLAN.md made true in code, then revised mid-run on Zach's report feedback: the concept is renamed 'highlighter' (JointJS terminology), stroke/mask join the pre-existing halo as first-class HighlighterKinds (stroke now the default), and the wire's message moved off an inline badge into the same hover Tooltip every other mark uses.
changes: apps/storybook-basics/src/components/diagnostic.tsx — new: the closed DiagnosticSeverity type, the Diagnostic interface (list, stable id — Zach's mid-run amendment over §1's original scalar), maxDiagnosticSeverity, diagnosticColorVar, diagnosticUnderlineStyle, DiagnosticTooltip (hover half), DiagnosticFlag (click half, Popover-based, carries a count)
apps/storybook-basics/src/components/popover.tsx — new: stock shadcn Popover over @base-ui/react/popover, copied verbatim the way tooltip.tsx/dropdown-menu.tsx already were

apps/storybook-basics/src/components/portEdge.tsx — PortEdgeItem grows diagnostics?, forwarded to the LabeledPort the default render draws
apps/storybook-basics/src/components/trace.tsx — diagnostics prop; one translucent backdrop <path> under the wire at max(severity), painted BEHIND the casing/hit/line (no sketched twin); info nothing

apps/storybook-basics/src/components/codeEditor.tsx + codeEditor.css — diagnostics?: CodeEditorDiagnostic[] (positional ranges, the one component that stays a list of ranges rather than max-severity); @codemirror/lint's setDiagnostics/linter; whole-field error also sets ariaInvalid; squiggle retinted from CM's hardcoded colours to this kit's three tokens via text-decoration
apps/storybook-basics/src/components/editableText.tsx — diagnostics prop; wavy/dotted underline on the rest span AND the editing control (EditableTextControl)
apps/storybook-basics/src/components/badge.tsx — new variant="warning" cva row (amber bg, dark text)

apps/storybook-basics/src/stories/Diagnostics.stories.tsx — new: 10 stories — one gallery per marked component, a wired+error channel-discipline proof, and a 'board with problems' composition

apps/storybook-basics/src/stories/CodeEditor.stories.tsx — Syntax Themes story's hardcoded #4f6ee5 fallback literals updated to var(--bbox-accent): porting that token in globals.css made the fallback chain resolve through the real token instead of past it, which is the intended effect of §2, not a regression

apps/storybook-basics/src/components/diagnostic.tsx -> highlighter.tsx (git mv) — Zach's report feedback: "Perhaps we can just borrow their terminology. Highlighters I think is right." Data stays `Diagnostic`; the drawing concept is now `HighlighterKind`.

highlighter.tsx — new HighlighterKind = "stroke" | "mask" | "halo" (Appendix A's JointJS table), DEFAULT_HIGHLIGHTER_KIND = "stroke", highlighterStrokeOutlineStyle (CSS outline) and highlighterMaskFrameStyle (the Minkowski-sum border-radius arithmetic — Appendix B's own "mask falls back to getBoundingClientRect() for HTML in a foreignObject" finding is why this is a bounding-rect technique, never a literal SVG <mask>)

port.tsx — highlighterKind prop; "stroke"/"mask" render the IDENTICAL crisp two-layer ring for a circle (documented why: no corners for mask to get more right than stroke), "halo" keeps the original translucent wash

block.tsx — highlighterKind prop; "stroke" = CSS outline (cheap, same radius as the box), "mask" = a sibling frame whose border-radius grows by the offset (genuinely equidistant), "halo" = the original glow, still error-only by default ("warning must not shout" stays specific to halo — stroke/mask mark both severities, since a crisp outline does not shout)

trace.tsx — highlighterKind prop ("mask" aliases to "stroke" for an open path — documented why); TraceBody's own output is now wrapped in DiagnosticTooltip so hovering a marked wire shows its message — replacing the plan's original "message rides TraceBadge" mock per Zach's own words: "I wonder if instead of display the error text directly on it, we instead follow the language of always showing the exact information in a pop out modal"
labeledPort.tsx, presets/value/value.tsx — highlighterKind forwarded through to Port/Block

stories/Diagnostics.stories.tsx — retitled "Diagnostics" -> "Styles/Diagnostics" (area:styles; CLAUDE.md's area vocabulary is closed and does not list "diagnostics", and CLAUDE.md is outside this lane's write set) with tags ["area:styles", "lane:invalid-states-impl"]; existing severity galleries pinned to highlighterKind="halo" where their captions/assertions specifically depended on the old default; new HighlighterKindsGallery story — the actual deliverable, all three kinds on one Block at one severity, side by side, with measured (not asserted) geometry proof
findings: Mid-run correction from the dispatcher: §1's ORIGINAL plan text specified a scalar `diagnostic?: Diagnostic`; the dispatcher overrode this to `diagnostics?: Diagnostic[]` with a stable `id` (Appendix B's convergence argument — a popover with 'the full anatomy' cannot show more than one finding from an already-merged scalar, and the flag's own COUNT cannot render from one). Verified against the actual plan doc on a peer worktree branch (component-docs-reorganize-8ce972 @ 0e47d91, 'Section 1 takes the list') — the override matches the settled, committed spec. Implemented as instructed: diagnostics is a list everywhere except CodeEditor, which was already positional-list-shaped in §5 and needed no change.

Mid-run constraint from the dispatcher: no src/skin/ imports and no sketched twins in the diagnostic chrome. Verified clean by grep across every touched file — every SketchOutline/sketchPathData/data-sketch reference in port.tsx/block.tsx/trace.tsx/badge.tsx/portEdge.tsx predates this work and belongs to those components' own base geometry; nothing I wrote calls into src/skin/ or emits a data-sketch twin. The Trace backdrop is one crisp <path>, not a crisp/sketch pair.

Real bug caught by the story play functions, not eyeballing: Port's halo initially painted for `info` too (any truthy severity, including "info", passed the old `if (diagnosticSeverity)` gate) — §5 says info paints NOTHING on a Port. Fixed with an explicit `!== "info"` guard; PortGallery's play function now asserts the info dot's box-shadow is byte-identical to the unmarked dot's.

Second bug caught the same way: my own BoardWithProblems/BlockGallery play functions queried `el.parentElement?.querySelector(flag-selector)` — since the flag is a CHILD of Block's own root (not a sibling), this cross-matched a DIFFERENT block's flag whenever two blocks shared an ancestor row. Fixed to query the block element's own subtree.

Channel discipline is measured, not asserted: PortGallery/WiredAndError compare the resolved `getComputedStyle().boxShadow` STRING before/after a diagnostic — the marked dot's box-shadow is asserted to be a strict superset (startsWith the unmarked one, longer, and the wired core's own background colour unchanged) rather than merely checking a class/attribute exists.

Discrepancy resolved between Block's row ('warning must not shout' — no glow) and ValueCapsule's row ('warning: amber glow'): added `diagnosticWarningGlow` (default false) to Block; ValueCapsule is the one caller that sets it, because a capsule has no flag to carry warning instead.

THE BIG ONE — a real, load-bearing bug the play-function gate could NOT catch, only a live capture did: the CodeEditor squiggle rendered at t=0 and then silently VANISHED by t=750ms, in every run. Root-caused with a live browser session (Claude_Browser tools), not guessed: @codemirror/lint's linter() mounts a ViewPlugin that unconditionally schedules `source(view)` to run ONCE, `delay`ms (default 750) after mount/any relevant update — not 'only on a real edit', which is what the original `cmLinter(() => [])` no-op-source comment assumed. At the 750ms mark it dispatched `setDiagnostics(state, [])`, erasing whatever the sync effect had written, because an empty-array-returning source is still an ACTIVE source. Fixed to `cmLinter(null)`: `lintConfig`'s own `combine` filters a `null` source out of `sources` entirely, so the scheduled `run()` finds `sources.length === 0` and dispatches nothing — the state field and its decorations still mount unconditionally either way. Verified with an in-page interval sampling the live DOM every 20ms for 3s post-fix: the marks now persist. `pnpm test-stories` passed BOTH before and after this fix — its play function asserts within ~50-100ms of mount, well inside the 750ms window, so it is not a sufficient acceptance gate for anything CodeMirror lints on a timer. This is exactly why the report mandate's 'open the rendered PNG and look at it' step exists.

Acceptance measured on this worktree (859ae8d baseline, NOT the 561b062/0e47d91 peer branch): pnpm --filter bbox-storybook-basics run typecheck clean; pnpm test-stories 46->47 files, 188->198 tests (both strictly above baseline); npx vitest --project=unit run 21 files/347 tests unchanged. All three re-verified AFTER the linter(null) fix, not just before.

Not done: a live Tooltip hover was not captured in this report (Base UI portals tooltip content to document.body on hover, which a static screenshot at page-load does not show) — the story play functions instead assert the DOM/CSS facts (box-shadow layers, text-decoration, aria-invalid, cm-lintRange classes) that the visual state is built from.

Zach's report feedback (vault PROJECT - Black Box UI.md:2589), relayed mid-run: the orthogonal axis, the diagnostics list with stable ids, and the text-mark treatment (@codemirror/lint + wavy underlines) are all CONFIRMED as-is — no changes made to any of that. Three changes requested: (1) rename to "highlighter" terminology, (2) add stroke/mask as first-class kinds alongside halo with stroke as the new default and a side-by-side comparison story, (3) move the wire's message off an inline badge into the pop-out Tooltip.

The stroke/mask distinction is only real where the shape has corners: verified live (getComputedStyle) that Block's mask frame measures border-radius 14px against the block's own 10px — exactly radius+offset(4), the Minkowski-sum arithmetic the code claims, not just asserted in a comment. For Port's circle, stroke and mask are documented as the IDENTICAL geometry (a circle has no corners to get more or less right) rather than building two indistinguishable rings.

The linter/edge-validation engine Zach also asked for is explicitly NOT this lane's work (the dispatcher is running it separately as pure functions over the scene) — nothing in this round imports or builds anything rule- or lint-shaped; `diagnostics` stays host-supplied data with no assumption about its producer.

Existing severity galleries (Port/LabeledPort/Block/ValueCapsule) were pinned to highlighterKind="halo" explicitly rather than left on the new default — their captions and play-function assertions were written against the old (now non-default) box-shadow-based treatment, and changing the default out from under them would have silently invalidated what they demonstrate. TraceGallery and BoardWithProblems needed no pinning: their assertions check element PRESENCE (the backdrop/flag exist), which holds under either kind, so they now exercise the new default live.

Acceptance on this worktree (859ae8d baseline): typecheck clean; pnpm test-stories 47 files / 199 tests (up from this lane's own prior commit at 47/198, and from the 859ae8d baseline's 46/188); vitest --project=unit 21 files / 347 tests unchanged. The coordinator separately reported the shared branch tip (a DIFFERENT, peer worktree) at 48 files/202 stories/442 unit tests — this worktree was not rebased onto it; these numbers are this lane's own delta against its own base commit.
